params.script_inline:
import sys, json
doc = json.load(sys.stdin)
hop = ((doc["envelope"].get("header") or {}).get("hop") or {})
name = str(hop.get("tool_name") or "")
asked = name if name else "(none)"
# The four tools this hive wires, named in the refusal. A model that asked for
# something else gets the LIST rather than a shrug: the vocabulary is closed,
# so naming it is the whole of the correction.
text = ("no tool named %s is wired into this builder. The tools are: "
        "librarian_search, catalogue_lookup, graph_read, registry_read." % asked)
sys.stdout.write(json.dumps({
    "header": {"route": "unknown", "operation": "unknown",
               "error_code": "unknown_tool", "tool_name": name,
               "tool_call_id": str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or "")},
    "messages": [{"origin": "tool", "type": "tool_result",
                  "id": str(hop.get("tool_call_id") or ""), "text": text}]}))

description.purpose: The guarded default of the builder's tool fan-out: a tool_call whose name no positive edge matched is answered as an ordinary tool_result under the id that asked, naming the four tools that do exist.
description.use_when: Never wired by hand and never addressed by name. Reached only when no positive tool edge fired, and only because the default edge's own guard held.
description.not_in_scope: Not a tool: no arguments are read, nothing is executed. No guess at a near-miss name either. And not a drain -- a cell that accepted the call and emitted nothing would be the swallowing sink GH #284 removed.
description.emits_meaning: route unknown: the lane the weave step folds a refusal back in on, distinct from the `tool_result` route the four wired eyes answer on, so the fan-in can count a refused call without mistaking it for a served one. hop.error_code is always `unknown_tool`; hop.tool_name is the name that was asked for -- verbatim, including the empty string when the call carried none; hop.tool_call_id is the id the fan-in is waiting on, and it is the whole reason this cell emits at all. messages[0] is ONE tool_result turn under that id, whose text names the asked-for tool and the closed vocabulary.
description.consumes_meaning: messages[]: the tool_call turn as it arrived. It is not parsed -- what the call wanted is irrelevant once there is nothing to serve it. hop.tool_name: the name that missed every positive edge, read only to be quoted back; its absence is a case, not an error.
examples: hop { tool_name: 'bash', tool_call_id: 'c-9' } -> tool_result id 'c-9' 'no tool named bash is wired into this builder. The tools are: librarian_search, catalogue_lookup, graph_read, registry_read.', hop { route: 'unknown', error_code: 'unknown_tool', tool_name: 'bash' }

hop { tool_call_id: 'c-10' } with no tool_name at all -> the same refusal under id 'c-10', tool_name empty and the text saying '(none)' -- the round closes and the composer learns its dispatcher lost the name, instead of the fan-in parking until the TTL runs out
